interactives.title: Interactive periodic table
interactives.sub: Colour all 118 elements by category, block, electronegativity, ionisation energy, radius or mass, and follow the trends.
interactives.note: IUPAC atomic weights, Pauling electronegativities, NIST ionisation energies and Cordero covalent radii, rounded.

interactives.title: Atomic structure explorer
interactives.sub: Add protons, neutrons and electrons to build elements, isotopes and ions, and check nuclear stability.
interactives.note: Shell (Bohr) picture for the first 20 elements; not to scale.

interactives.title: Electron configuration builder
interactives.sub: Fill orbital boxes for any element up to krypton, checked against Aufbau, Pauli and Hund, including the Cr and Cu exceptions.
interactives.note: Ground states of neutral atoms up to Z = 36.

interactives.title: Atomic orbitals
interactives.sub: Hydrogen's 1s to 3d orbitals from the exact wavefunctions: density slices with phase, 3D probability clouds and radial distributions.
interactives.note: Exact for hydrogen; many-electron atoms have similar shapes but different sizes and energies.

interactives.title: Ionic and covalent bonding
interactives.sub: Dot-and-cross diagrams for ionic compounds and covalent molecules, with electronegativity differences and partial charges.
interactives.note: Electronegativity cut-offs are a rule of thumb; bonding is a continuum.

interactives.title: Lewis structure builder
interactives.sub: Set bond orders and lone pairs; the checker counts electrons, checks octets and shows formal charges and resonance.
interactives.note: Octet rule with the usual exceptions (H, B, expanded octets in period 3).

interactives.title: VSEPR molecular geometry
interactives.sub: Build any combination of bonding pairs and lone pairs in 3D and see the electron-domain geometry, shape and bond angles.
interactives.note: Ideal VSEPR geometries; measured angles quoted for H₂O and NH₃.

interactives.title: Molecular polarity
interactives.sub: Bond dipoles add as vectors over the 3D shape: see why CO₂ and CCl₄ are non-polar but H₂O and CHCl₃ are polar.
interactives.note: Qualitative dipoles from electronegativity differences; real dipole moments also depend on lone pairs and bond lengths.

interactives.title: Intermolecular forces
interactives.sub: Compare boiling points across alkanes, noble gases, hydrides, alcohols and isomers to see dispersion forces and hydrogen bonding.
interactives.note: Measured normal boiling points, rounded from standard tables.

interactives.title: 3D molecular model viewer
interactives.sub: Turn and zoom 25 molecules or type your own SMILES: ball-and-stick or space-filling, with formula and molar mass.
interactives.note: Geometry from a simple in-browser force field: good shapes and stereochemistry, approximate bond lengths.

interactives.title: Organic functional group explorer
interactives.sub: Find and highlight the functional groups in molecules from ethanol to caffeine, or in any SMILES you type.
interactives.note: Groups found by substructure rules on the molecular graph.

interactives.title: Stereochemistry and chirality explorer
interactives.sub: Put each molecule beside its mirror image and try to superimpose them; decide which are chiral.
interactives.note: Models from the in-browser force field.

interactives.title: R/S configuration exercise
interactives.sub: Rank the groups at a stereocentre by CIP priority, turn the model and assign R or S.
interactives.note: Simplified CIP rules that cover textbook cases.

interactives.title: E/Z isomerism exercise
interactives.sub: Rank the groups on each end of a double bond and decide whether the isomer is E or Z.
interactives.note: Simplified CIP rules that cover textbook cases.

interactives.title: Curly-arrow mechanism builder
interactives.sub: Draw every arrow in SN2, electrophilic addition, nucleophilic addition and E2 mechanisms, step by step.
interactives.note: Standard textbook mechanisms; 2D schematic structures.

interactives.title: SN1 versus SN2
interactives.sub: Vary the substrate, nucleophile and solvent and compare the two mechanisms' rates and stereochemical outcomes.
interactives.note: Qualitative model with order-of-magnitude relative rates; elimination is only described.

interactives.title: Organic synthesis pathway builder
interactives.sub: Plan multi-step routes between functional groups with real reagents and conditions, lengthening chains with cyanide.
interactives.note: Standard A-level and first-year reactions; real syntheses have many alternatives.

interactives.title: Reaction energy profiles
interactives.sub: Set Ea and ΔH, add an intermediate, and see the fraction of molecules with enough energy at any temperature.
interactives.note: Exact Maxwell–Boltzmann energy fractions; the shaded plot uses a compressed energy axis.

interactives.title: Equilibrium and Le Chatelier
interactives.sub: Run reversible reactions to equilibrium, then change concentration, volume or temperature and watch Q return to K.
interactives.note: Mass-action kinetics with illustrative K values; van 't Hoff temperature dependence.

interactives.title: Acids, bases and pH
interactives.sub: Exact pH for strong and weak acids at any concentration, species distributions, and buffers.
interactives.note: Exact charge-balance solution; activities taken as concentrations.

interactives.title: Titration simulator
interactives.sub: Titrate strong and weak acids and a weak base drop by drop, choose indicators and read equivalence points and pKa.
interactives.note: Exact pH curves from the charge balance; ideal solutions.

interactives.title: Electrochemical cells
interactives.sub: Build cells from 13 half-cells: anode and cathode, E°cell, the Nernst equation, ΔG° and K.
interactives.note: Standard electrode potentials from standard tables; concentrations as activities.

interactives.title: Gibbs free energy and spontaneity
interactives.sub: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS for real reactions: find where they become spontaneous and what K is at any temperature.
interactives.note: Standard ΔH° and ΔS° at 298 K, assumed constant with temperature.

interactives.title: Reaction kinetics
interactives.sub: Zero-, first- and second-order rate laws, integrated plots, half-lives, a mystery order to identify, and the Arrhenius equation.
interactives.note: Exact integrated rate laws; the mystery data include simulated noise.

interactives.title: Catalysis
interactives.sub: Lower the activation energy with a catalyst and see how the fraction of successful collisions, and the rate, rise.
interactives.note: Exact Maxwell–Boltzmann fractions; the energy plot is schematic.

interactives.title: Spectroscopy problems
interactives.sub: Identify unknowns from their molecular formula, IR spectrum, ¹H NMR spectrum and mass spectrum together.
interactives.note: Simulated spectra from correlation data (see the IR, NMR and MS labs).

interactives.title: Infrared spectrum viewer
interactives.sub: IR spectra of 12 compounds with their diagnostic bands labelled, including the fingerprint region.
interactives.note: Simulated from characteristic absorption ranges, not measured spectra.

interactives.title: ¹H NMR interpretation
interactives.sub: Chemical shifts, integration and n + 1 splitting for 12 compounds, with every signal assigned.
interactives.note: Typical shifts with first-order splitting at 400 MHz.

interactives.title: Mass spectrometry and fragmentation
interactives.sub: Molecular ions, exact isotope patterns for chlorine and bromine, and the fragment ions behind the base peaks.
interactives.note: Isotope patterns calculated from natural abundances; fragment heights approximate.

interactives.title: Molecular docking and binding
interactives.sub: Fit ligands into a binding pocket by hand or by auto-docking, scoring hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, a salt bridge and clashes.
interactives.note: Invented pocket and ligands; a teaching scoring function, not a prediction.
